Lab Validation Runbook - Magnetic Circuit, Rev A
Synthetic hackathon engineering evidence
1. Wiring and references
Connect the exciting coil with the documented polarity dot orientation.
Connect the measuring coil so its recorded induced voltage is negative relative to the positive air-gap flux arrow.
Confirm electrical ground and magnetic ground are instantiated in the simulation model.
Use the nominal 1.50 mm gap for AV-11. The 1.58 mm shim value belongs to the as-built prototype comparison only.
2. Excitation
Apply 50 Hz quasi-static excitation with an RMS current-phasor magnitude ramp: 0 A until 0.10 s, linear ramp to 2.0 A by 0.50 s, then hold to 1.0 s.
3. Expected trends
Signal | Expected behavior
N*I | Linear ramp with current
Phi_core | Linear ramp under linear reluctance
Phi_gap | 0.92*Phi_core
Phi_leak | 0.08*Phi_core
B and H | Linear ramp
Exciting induced-voltage magnitude | Linear ramp; positive orientation
Measuring induced-voltage magnitude | Linear ramp; negative orientation
4. Common errors
Using 2.0 A as a peak rather than RMS phasor magnitude causes a sqrt(2) mismatch.
Using the as-built 1.58 mm gap in the nominal verification changes the flux and invalidates the AV-11 comparison.
Applying total core flux to the air gap instead of useful flux ignores leakage and overpredicts air-gap B.
Omitting one of the grounds can leave the corresponding potential reference undefined.
